title: New Report from Informa TechTarget Identifies Key Shifts in B2B Technology Purchase Journeys Driven by AI, Buying Groups, and Evolving Media Habits
summary: New research finds that AI’s influence changes throughout the purchase journey, playing a larger role in the mid-funnel research and evaluation stage (44%) than in discovery (33%) or decision-making (20%). Six in 10 buying groups
body_markdown:
- New research finds that AI’s influence changes throughout the purchase journey, playing a larger role in the mid-funnel research and evaluation stage (44%) than in discovery (33%) or decision-making (20%).
- Six in 10 buying groups have changed shape in the past two years, with many adding business and technical stakeholders, and 27% of buyers cite lack of buy-in from business decision-makers as a top cause of purchase delays.
- Buyers named information sources typically treated as brand awareness vehicles among their top vendor discovery sources, including newsletters (46%) and independent media (41%), outranking both AI tools (33%) and vendor outreach (31%).


Informa TechTarget (NASDAQ:[TTGT](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVrGAbmtCSbtzK9BhcdVANUFHnMWB7N4V_ZML2-xoZw_lGTArdHydTr3EodPi-VOh646amY3OuykaHhN470_8Fck9K5lqJHt7kZ4edeIyE7zoqG9kW4opPB50m8p-mqIx5qM8Mhj_UydfThg) )—an indispensable partner for B2B intelligence, media, and marketing solutions—today announced the findings of its B2B Content Engagement & Buyer Behavior Report, which examines how B2B and enterprise technology buyers find, evaluate, and choose the solutions that power their businesses. Formerly known as the Media Consumption Study, this year’s survey of B2B technology buyers expanded its focus on factors beyond media engagement that impact enterprise technology and B2B purchase decisions, including the growing influence of artificial intelligence and the expansion of the buying group within organizations. Survey responses from approximately 500 global technology buyers told a consistent story across content, channels, AI, and the buying process itself—one that demonstrates the purchase journey has fundamentally shifted in ways that many marketing funnels and dashboards do not yet match.


“Findings in the B2B Content Engagement and Buyer Behavior Report should challenge some long-held assumptions about how B2B marketers build brands and measure campaigns. The modern B2B purchase journey has been fundamentally changed by AI and shifting buying group dynamics; and brand and demand need to work together in a way that most go-to-market strategies still haven’t shifted to accommodate,” said Staci M. Gullotta, Chief Marketing Officer, Informa TechTarget. “At Informa TechTarget, we help our clients move beyond tracking individual leads and disconnected campaigns to a more unified approach that strengthens brand authority in the age of AI and drives measurable business growth.”


The B2B Content Engagement & Buyer Behavior Study is designed to give B2B go-to-market teams insight into the preferences and behaviors of B2B technology buyers. With insight-driven practical takeaways and recommendations woven throughout, the report is intended to help marketers formulate better strategies and plans to improve the effectiveness of their marketing programs. It provides data deep dives into a number of specific and interconnected topics, including content and channel preferences, artificial intelligence, newsletters, vendor content, webinars and video content, industry events, buying committees, and reasons for stalled deals.


Available today, the report identifies several key findings about how B2B purchase decision-making is shifting, including:


- **AI visibility earns consideration, not trust:** AI is now a top-three source during active research, and 58% of buyers ‘often’ or ‘very often’ click through when it cites a vendor. Yet only 42% say a citation builds trust—a 16-point drop from click to confidence. And the bigger the decision, the further AI moves from it. For investments topping $1 million, nearly a third (30%) of buyers don’t use AI to guide decisions at all. “No amount of AI model optimization will make AI reflect credibility you haven’t built,” said Lieu Thi Pham, VP of Strategy, Brand and Content at Informa TechTarget, and lead architect of the company’s[B2B AI Authority Index](https://www.informatechtarget.com/interactive/b2b-ai-authority/?utm_source=PR&utm_medium=ITT&utm_campaign=new-report-from-informa-techtarget-identifies-key-shifts-in-b2b-technology-purchase-journeys-driven-by-ai-buying-groups-and-evolving-media-habits) . “On the decisions that matter most, buyers take the question straight to the sources they already trust.”
- **AI content needs a human perspective:** Seventy-two percent of buyers believe half or more of what they read is AI-generated, and 61% say high-quality vendor content is hard to find. Buyers cite reliable expertise (60%), objectivity (57%), pain point relevancy (55%), and source credibility (53%) among their top priorities when choosing an information source. “Buyers value AI for high-level information gathering (64%), but they ultimately trust what a machine can’t fake: unique data and insights, and a point of view only thought leaders and subject matter experts possess. “Polished, competent content is now the baseline, however it was made. What stands out is what only you can bring: your data, your experts, and a point of view you’ll defend,” added Thi Pham.
- **Buying committees continue to expand beyond IT:** Six in 10 buying teams have changed shape in the past two years, with many adding business (31%) and technical (28%) stakeholders. For the second consecutive year, nearly half (48%) of buyers describe the purchase decision process as collaborative, and 24% say they now spend more time discussing solutions internally. With ‘ROI uncertainty’ (30%), ‘lack of in-house expertise’ (29%), and ‘lack of buy-in from business decision-makers’ (27%) cited among the top internal factors that delay purchases, vendors that reach and equip the full buying group early stand to move deals forward faster.
- **Brand awareness sources fuel vendor discovery:** Newsletters (46%) are the number one most cited vendor discovery channel in the study, and 74% of buyers receive four or more professional newsletters a week. Independent media (41%) ranks third for discovery, just behind the second most popular option of web search (43%). Typically categorized as “brand” or “communications,” these editorial media channels are harder to tie directly to conversion. This creates a familiar budget problem: effective preference-building channels can end up underfunded despite their key role in influencing demand.


The report is based on responses from 499 global B2B technology buyers involved in evaluating or purchasing technology solutions for their organizations, all of whom are opted-in members of Informa TechTarget’s global audience ecosystem, which includes hundreds of award-winning media titles such as Dark Reading, Computer World, and Channel Dive, and BrightTALK webinar communities. Survey respondents span the full seniority range—from C-suite to staff-level buyers, with Networking & Infrastructure, Information Technology, Security, and Data & Analytics among the most represented departments—whose companies range in size from fewer than 100 to 10,000 or more employees.


B2B marketing, sales, and other go-to-market professionals interested in the complete findings can access the full report[here](https://www.informatechtarget.com/research-analysis/content-engagement-buyer-behavior/?utm_source=PR&utm_medium=ITT&utm_campaign=new-report-from-informa-techtarget-identifies-key-shifts-in-b2b-technology-purchase-journeys-driven-by-ai-buying-groups-and-evolving-media-habits) .
